summary: Safety-sentinel: preflight and hotpatch plan for tenant optimizer profile causing sporadic tail latency
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightHealth AI reported a sudden increase in 95th/99th percentile tail latency for inference requests after applying a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that enabled aggressive batching, prefix KV prefetch, and a mixed 4-bit quantization profile. Impact: Intermittent API timeouts (up to 30s) affecting live features for 10% of requests, SLO breaches for the customer's dedicated pool. Environment: Dedicated tenant cluster in us-west-2; production traffic; tenant ID bhai-03. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use tenant API key bhai-03 in prod us-west-2. 2) Send typical 1-2k concurrent short-chat requests (avg seq len 120 tokens) over 2–5 minutes. 3) Observe increasing 95p/99p latency and occasional 504s. Observed behavior: Gradual buildup of host-level GPU memory pressure during steady traffic, periodic long-running server-side stalls that correlate with aggressive batch formation and KV prefetch spikes. Expected behavior: Stable p95/p99 for same workload after optimizer change with small improvements in median latency. Logs/metrics: - Serving runtime trace: intermittent block on batch-assembly loop (trace id included in comment) - Console metrics: burst in batch size to >2.5x configured target, KV prefetch cache hit ratio drops to 0.6 briefly - Example request ids: req_bhai_20260312_01..05 - No obvious OOMs in node-level logs; GC spikes on host reported. Initial hypothesis: Combination of larger-than-expected batching window + KV prefetch thrash causing temporary memory overhead and kernel scheduling stalls on GPU, accentuated by mixed 4-bit quant path. Temporary mitigations already applied: - Switched tenant traffic to conservative optimizer profile (via console rollback toggle) which reduced incidents but customer reports stateful sessions lost for some in-flight requests. - Applied traffic-split to route 10% to old profile for safety. Customer asks for: 1) a reproducible preflight checklist to validate optimizer profiles before tenant-wide promotion, 2) a safe, tenant-scoped hotpatch rollback procedure that preserves in-flight session continuity where possible, and 3) suggestions for configuration guardrails to prevent recurrence. Recommended action (short term): 1) Run the "safety-sentinel" preflight on a shadow workload: use the customer's representative prompt set (attached) against a staging pool configured to mimic dedicated pool (same GPU instance types & quant kernels). 2) Execute the following hotpatch rollback steps (tenant-scoped, staged):   a) Pause new session-creation at load-balancer for bhai-03 for 30s window.   b) Set optimizer profile to conservative snapshot (profile id: conservative-2026-02) via tenant-scoped API — this toggles batching window to 20ms, disables KV prefetch, and uses baseline 8-bit quant fallback.   c) Gradually re-open session creation and split traffic 80/20 (new/old) for 10 minutes, monitor p95/p99, batch-size distribution, KV hit ratio, GPU utilization.   d) If metrics stabilize, shift to 50/50 for 5 minutes then 100% over 15 minutes.   e) If any regression occurs, immediately reapply traffic-split back to 90% conservative and open an incident. 3) Provide a one-line hotpatch CLI command and a console playbook snippet for the customer's SRE (included in comments). Recommended action (long term): 1) Introduce a tenant-level optimizer preflight job that runs shadowed traffic for 10–15 minutes and validates thresholds for p95/p99, cache hit ratio, and batch size variance before allowing promotion. 2) Add a guardrail rule in the console that prevents promoting mixed-4bit profiles to dedicated pool without a preflight sign-off. 3) Capture optimizer profile snapshots automatically to enable atomic revert per-tenant. Post-action verifications: 1) Monitor 1h after full rollback for p99 stability and error rates. 2) Run a regression eval on the attached prompt set to ensure output quality isn't materially degraded by fallback quant profile. Follow-ups/future work: - Engineering to investigate kernel scheduling interaction with mixed-4bit execution path (link to PR). - Product to consider UI change for safer profile promotion. Attachments: representative prompt set (prompts_v1.json), sample traces (trace_ids list in comments).
